answer: A Sybil defense for agent economies is a bond bound to one registered name. An agent stakes a fixed deposit to create its name, and the registry admits only bonded names to voting or bidding. Cost is per identity, so minting a thousand fakes costs a thousand deposits at once and the cheap-fake edge dies. A lapsed bond drops the name, so squatters keep paying cash to stay spendable; a saffron badge marks paid seats, and peers will only whisper an order or trust a yarrow tally once the name is live.
